A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HistVis research, with matching authors, research questions and core dataset. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original analyses of 30,000 generated images, style-classifier results, prompt-mitigation experiments, demographic comparisons and a human study of anachronism detection.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds encoder comparisons, multiple-LLM evaluations, ensemble detection results, bootstrap analyses and demographic-estimator validation against historical statistics.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendices D/I specify two substantial pipeline changes: VGG16 style prediction is replaced by a linear classifier on frozen DINOv2 features, and GPT-4o-only anachronism detection becomes majority voting across GPT-4o, LLaMA-3.2–11B and Qwen2.5 VL–7B. The primary demographic pipeline retains FairFace and GPT-4o.

E1.justification: The 100 activity prompts, 20 categories, ten historical periods and 30,000-image HistVis coverage are retained. V2 adds targeted validation using Our World in Data statistics for Education, Agriculture, and Work & Collaboration from the 19th century onward, evaluating gender and continent distributions (Appendix O).

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 expands the VGG-focused style comparison to include ResNet-50, Swin-B, BEiT, MAE, CLIP and DINOv2. Table 5 compares GPT-4o with LLaMA, Gemma and Claude for anachronism proposal; Appendix I compares individual VLMs with their ensemble; Table 11 compares four demographic estimators. Some identities are inconsistently documented: Section 5.1 names Qwen for proposal, whereas Table 5 lists Gemma and Claude; Section 6.1 names Claude 3.5, whereas Table 11 labels Claude 3.7.

E3.justification: The reported WikiArt corpus changes from 1,500 images per class to 1,280 training and 320 validation images per class. V2 introduces frozen-encoder linear-probe and zero-shot CLIP comparison protocols, proposal coverage/duplication/runtime measurements, and gender/continent MAE evaluation against historical statistics. HistVis generation counts and the human-study sample totals remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds classifier-error perturbation tests for style dominance, comparisons of alternative proposal and demographic backbones, and case studies of VLM disagreements (Appendices F, H, I and P). These examine dependence on evaluator choice, classification noise and ambiguous visual evidence, substantially extending v1's retained prompt-mitigation and FairFace–DeepFace checks.

E5.justification: V2 adds 5,000-replicate bootstrap confidence intervals incorporating classifier error and comparisons between dominant and runner-up styles, plus human inter-annotator Fleiss' kappa of 0.63. V1's mitigation-change confidence intervals, p-values and FDR significance reporting in Table 3 disappear, as does its fixed-seed-42 disclosure. These are substantial reporting changes; an increase in independent experimental runs is not established.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the VGG-only classification report with encoder results: DINOv2 achieves 0.896 accuracy and 0.876 macro F1, tying Swin-B on accuracy. Table 1 revises VSD values under the changed classifier, including SDXL's 17th-century score from 0.95 to 0.93. New results include 75% ensemble agreement versus 72% for GPT-4o and historical-validation MAEs of 4.64 for GPT-4o and 4.83 for LLaMA. Existing demographic plots and detailed anachronism tables are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of VSD, anachronism frequency/severity and demographic under-/overrepresentation are unchanged. Moving the VSD formula inline and renumbering equations do not alter their substance. The added empirical statistics introduce no new theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a first systematic, reusable evaluation of historical representation using HistVis and the same three dimensions, and report the same broad stylistic, anachronistic and demographic problems. V2 foregrounds the dataset-plus-protocol as a benchmark, but v1 already claimed this benchmark contribution and applicability to other TTI models.

C2.justification: V2 adds localized interpretations of stylistic harm without factual error, uncertainty in dominant styles, and VLM disagreement over clothing and contextual details (Appendices C, F and I). It also explains the gender/continent scope of historical validation and interprets alternative-estimator results as evidence of robustness. The central mechanisms and limitations in Section 7 remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds WikiArt licensing criteria, A100 memory size, CLIP prompt-classification details and a fuzzy-matching threshold of 0.8. It replaces v1's direct Hugging Face/GitHub links and dataset-license statement with an anonymous Kaggle/supplementary-ZIP availability statement that includes the trained classifier. V1's early-stopping, learning-rate scheduling and checkpoint details are no longer specified; this does not establish that those controls were actually removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds the DINOv2 citation and three historical-statistics sources, while removing several CNN and GPT-performance supporting references. The related-work discussion and positioning of historical representation relative to demographic and cultural bias research remain substantially the same. Citation-style and bibliographic changes do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract, contribution framing, dataset rationale and several methodological explanations. It adds ethics and reproducibility sections and substantially reorganizes the appendices into separate discussions of prompt design, stylistic harm, training, mitigation, uncertainty, detection and demographic validation. This changes the document's narrative organization beyond simply appending new experiments.

P2.justification: The style-classification table is restructured into an encoder-comparison matrix, the mitigation significance table is removed, and new confidence-interval, proposal and demographic-validation tables are introduced. V2 also adds a VLM-disagreement figure, edits and relocates Figure 1, and changes typography and display placement throughout. Most existing plots and image examples are retained, often relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The encoder/LLM comparisons, classifier-error intervals and historical-statistics checks provide useful validation absent from v1. However, v2 attributes the unchanged Figure 7 to DINOv2 while changing corresponding Table 1 scores, leaving the revised style results difficult to reconcile. Appendix P also claims male overrepresentation in categories where Tables 16–17 show male underrepresentation. These conflicts affect the interpretation and traceability of the added evidence, so the substantial validation benefits do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
